# CLI reference

<!-- Generated by tools/docs.py from the code. Don't edit it by hand. -->

Every command of `wm` 0.1.0. Read commands take `--json`; their payloads are described in the [JSON schema reference](json.md).

Exit codes: `0` success; `1` refused, or problems found; `2` usage error.

## wm init

Create the record in this git repository.

```
wm init [--atlas NAME] [--tool NAME]
```

- `--atlas`: make this repository an atlas: a record that several code repos share
- `--tool`: an agent tool to set up; repeatable (default: claude-code)

## wm update

Migrate the record to this version and regenerate the files Waymark owns.

```
wm update
```

## wm doctor

Check wm, git and this project's setup; changes nothing.

```
wm doctor [--json]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version

## wm git-hooks

Put the committed git hooks in this repository and point this clone's git at them.

```
wm git-hooks
```

## wm run-hook

Run one of the git hooks' checks; the hooks call this.

```
wm run-hook <commit-msg|pre-commit> [file]
```

- `name`: one of `commit-msg`, `pre-commit`
- `file`: the commit message file (commit-msg only)

## wm ci

Add a GitHub Actions workflow that installs the pinned wm and runs wm check.

```
wm ci
```

## wm pr

Describe a pull request from a change: its title and description.

```
wm pr [--json] <change> [--repo NAME]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version
- `change`: the change's name
- `--repo`: in an atlas, the code repo it is for

## wm atlas

Register atlases on this machine, point code repos at them, check their setup.

```
wm atlas <command>
```

## wm atlas register

Register this atlas on this machine, with its code repos found through their path hints, or one code repo at a folder.

```
wm atlas register [repo] [folder]
```

- `repo`: a code repo's name, from the atlas's settings
- `folder`: that code repo's folder

## wm atlas point

Write the pointer file that tells this code repo which atlas holds its record.

```
wm atlas point <atlas> [--path FOLDER]
```

- `atlas`: the atlas's name
- `--path`: the atlas's folder, relative to this repository's top

## wm atlas doctor

Check this atlas's registry entries, code repos, branches and pins; changes nothing.

```
wm atlas doctor [--json]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version

## wm hook

Answer an agent tool's hook event, read as JSON from standard input.

```
wm hook <tool> <event>
```

- `tool`: the agent tool whose hook this is
- `event`: the tool's name for the event

## wm new

Create a change, milestone or exploration from the built-in template.

```
wm new <change|milestone|exploration> <name> [--short] [--owner NAME]
```

- `kind`: one of `change`, `milestone`, `exploration`
- `name`: a kebab-case name, for example add-search-limit
- `--short`: put a change on the short path
- `--owner`: a change's owner (default: your git name)

## wm accept

Accept a change, so its items can be applied. For the human to run.

```
wm accept <change>
```

- `change`: the change's name

## wm tick

Tick an item: it has been applied.

```
wm tick <change> <item>
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `item`: the item's number, for example 1.2

## wm block

Record that an item is blocked.

```
wm block <change> <item> <reason>
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `item`: the item's number, for example 1.2
- `reason`: why it is blocked

## wm gap

Record a spec gap: the record wasn't enough to build an item.

```
wm gap <change> <item> <note>
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `item`: the item's number, for example 1.2
- `note`: what is missing from the record

## wm review

Record a self-review of an item.

```
wm review <change> <item> --self SUMMARY
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `item`: the item's number, for example 1.2
- `--self`: what the review checked and found (required)

## wm verdict

Record a reviewer's verdict on an item.

```
wm verdict <change> <item> <pass|changes|spec-gap> <reasons>
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `item`: the item's number, for example 1.2
- `verdict`: one of `pass`, `changes`, `spec-gap`
- `reasons`: the reviewer's reasons

## wm reopen

Reopen an item after a review asked for changes.

```
wm reopen <change> <item>
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `item`: the item's number, for example 1.2

## wm resolve

Record what was decided about an item that went to the human, and free it.

```
wm resolve <change> <item> <decision>
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `item`: the item's number, for example 1.2
- `decision`: what was decided

## wm sync

Merge an applied change's deltas into the specs without archiving it.

```
wm sync <change>
```

- `change`: the change's name

## wm archive

Archive an applied change. For the human to run.

```
wm archive <change> [--outcome TEXT] [--override REASON]
```

- `change`: the change's name
- `--outcome`: what came of the change
- `--override`: archive although review records are missing; the reason is recorded

## wm close

Close a milestone whose changes are all archived.

```
wm close <milestone>
```

- `milestone`: the milestone's name

## wm status

Show where things stand: changes, milestones, what needs you.

```
wm status [--json]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version

## wm inbox

Show what only the human can resolve.

```
wm inbox [--json]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version

## wm show

Show everything about one change, spec, milestone or exploration.

```
wm show [--json] <name> [--kind KIND] [--from ATLAS]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version
- `name`: its name; an archived change also by its dated folder name
- `--kind`: which kind, if the name is shared; one of `change`, `spec`, `milestone`, `exploration`
- `--from`: read a spec from an atlas this project references

## wm ls

List changes, specs, milestones or explorations.

```
wm ls [--json] <changes|specs|milestones|explorations> [--archived] [--from ATLAS]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version
- `kind`: one of `changes`, `specs`, `milestones`, `explorations`
- `--archived`: include archived changes or milestones
- `--from`: list the specs of an atlas this project references

## wm instructions

Say what to do at a step of a change: the file, its template, the rules, the commands.

```
wm instructions [--json] [explore|propose|specs|design|tasks|apply|review|archive] [--change NAME]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version
- `step`: the step (default: the change's next step); one of `explore`, `propose`, `specs`, `design`, `tasks`, `apply`, `review`, `archive`
- `--change`: the change (default: the only one)

## wm context

Print the context pack for exploring, or for implementing or reviewing one item.

```
wm context [--json] [change] [item] --for ROLE
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version
- `change`: the change's name
- `item`: the item's number, for example 1.2
- `--for`: the job the pack is for; one of `explore`, `implement`, `review` (required)

## wm check

Check the record's health: format, links, conflicts, evidence.

```
wm check [--json]
```

- `--json`: print the view as JSON, with its schema version
